grammar_concept.title: Fronting for Emphasis
grammar_concept.rule: In formal or literary English, an object, complement, or adverbial phrase can be moved to the front of the sentence to emphasise it, ahead of the subject. Unlike negative-adverbial inversion, the subject and verb usually keep their normal order after a fronted object or complement — only the element being emphasised moves.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Fronting is about word order, not verb form: instead of 'I cannot accept this', you say 'This I cannot accept' — the object 'this' moves to the front, but 'I cannot accept' stays in normal order. It's a stylistic tool for formal writing, speeches and literary register, used to highlight the most important idea in the sentence.
grammar_concept.example: This I cannot accept. Such was the level of noise that nobody could concentrate. Gone are the days when a handshake was enough.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Isto não posso aceitar. Tal era o nível de ruído que ninguém conseguia concentrar-se. Já lá vão os dias em que um aperto de mão era suficiente.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Falantes de português tendem a não reconhecer a fronting como uma estrutura deliberada e a tentar traduzi-la literalmente sem perceber a função enfática, ou a evitá-la por completo em produção, mesmo quando o registo formal a pede.
grammar_concept.correction: Para dar ênfase formal a um objeto ou complemento, coloca-o no início da frase — o resto da frase mantém, regra geral, a ordem normal sujeito-verbo ("This I cannot accept", não "This cannot I accept").
grammar_concept.real_world_example: In a formal speech: "Such was the impact of the discovery that the entire field of research changed direction."

vocabulary.definition_en: a powerful effect that something has on a situation or person
example_sentences: The report had a significant impact on public opinion.
Such was the startling nature of the news that no one spoke for a minute.
Wholeheartedly do I agree with this proposal.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the fronted version: "I cannot accept this." → "___ I cannot accept."
exercises.explanation: "This" (o objeto) move-se para o início — o resto ("I cannot accept") mantém a ordem normal.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Tentar inverter também o sujeito e o verbo ("This cannot I accept"), aplicando por engano a regra de inversão de advérbios negativos a este caso diferente.

exercises.prompt: Complete: ___ was the level of noise that nobody could concentrate.
exercises.explanation: "Such was the level of noise that..." é uma estrutura fixa de fronting com "such" + substantivo, seguida de "that" para a consequência.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "So" em vez de "Such" — "so" pede um adjetivo ("so noisy that"), "such" pede um substantivo ("such noise that").

exercises.explanation: "Startling" significa surpreendente ou chocante, algo que apanha alguém desprevenido.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What does the speaker say is now gone?
correct_answer: the days when a handshake was enough
the era of simple handshake deals
exercises.explanation: No áudio: "Gone are the days when a handshake was enough to seal a deal."
exercises.transcript: Gone are the days when a handshake was enough to seal a deal — everything now needs to be in writing.

exercises.prompt: Read: "Wholeheartedly do I support this initiative, and I urge the board to approve it without delay." What is the writer's attitude to the initiative?
exercises.explanation: "Wholeheartedly do I support" e "urge... without delay" mostram apoio forte e claro.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English (usando fronting): "Tal foi o impacto da descoberta que toda a área de investigação mudou de direção."
correct_answer: Such was the impact of the discovery that the entire field of research changed direction.
exercises.explanation: "Such was the impact...that" é a tradução direta da estrutura enfática com "tal foi...que" do português.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir literalmente sem usar fronting ("The impact of the discovery was such that...") não está errado, mas perde a ênfase formal do original colocado no início.

steps.content: The fronted element carries the main sentence stress, since it's the whole point of the structure: "THIS I cannot accept", "SUCH was the impact..." — without stress on the fronted word, the emphasis effect is lost entirely.

steps.prompt: Use fronting to emphasise a strong opinion — e.g. 'This I firmly believe...' or 'Such was the effect that...' about something you feel strongly about.
Write 3 formal sentences using fronting to emphasise different elements (an object, a degree with 'such', and an adverbial like 'gone are the days').
